recall_prompt: Say how you would simplify this product without expanding a cube.
insider_note: Pair one (1 − i) with (1 + i) before touching the cube: that pair is the real number 2, and what is left is only (1 − i)². Expanding the cube term by term is longer and is where the sign slips happen.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Regroup the factors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Take one factor (1 − i) out of the cube and pair it with (1 + i): that pair is a conjugate product, which is real. What remains is (1 − i)², a small square.

recall.must_convey: That the product is regrouped as (1 − i)² times (1 − i)(1 + i), giving (1 − 2i + i²)(1 − i²).
accept: take one factor of one minus i and pair it with one plus i, leaving one minus i squared
regroup as one minus i squared times one minus i into one plus i
use the conjugate pair one minus i into one plus i which is one minus i squared
oka one minus i ni one plus i tho pair chesi, migilindi one minus i square
split the cube into a square and a conjugate product

steps.why: Expanding (1 − i)³ directly is four terms and two powers of i. Pairing one factor with its conjugate gives a real number at once, and (1 − i)² is one line — the regrouping is what keeps a 2-mark question at 2 marks of work.
common_mistakes: Expanding the cube term by term and losing a sign.
Writing (1 − i)(1 + i) as 1 + i² instead of 1 − i².

steps.label: Simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. i² = −1 makes the first bracket −2i and the second bracket 2. Then the real part is 0.

recall.must_convey: That with i² = −1 the product is (−2i)(2) = −4i, which is 0 + i(−4).
accept: the first bracket is minus two i and the second is two so the product is minus four i
minus two i times two equals minus four i, real part zero and imaginary part minus four
it comes to zero plus i times minus four
i square minus one pettithe minus two i into two, that is minus four i
the answer is minus four i, a is zero and b is minus four

steps.why: The form a + ib must show both parts, even when one is zero. Writing 0 + i(−4) says a = 0 and b = −4 explicitly, which is what 'express in the form a + ib' asks.
common_mistakes: Writing (1 − i²) as 0 by using i² = +1.
